This is probably the most beautiful game I've ever played. It really is something special. The story, maps, puzzles, and music/sound design are all amazing. I love both the base game and the DLC, although I know some people do get spooked by the DLC.

The game has a sci-fi theme, but I think it has a universal appeal that transcends the genre that anyone would appreciate. Just make sure to take in everything and carefully read what the game tells you. There's not a lot to read, and all of it comes together wonderfully. Although reading things is important, the ship log nicely summarizes anything you've read, so don't worry about memorizing everything you've read.

And most importantly, avoid spoilers. This game is essentially a carefully crafted escape room. Spoilers don't just ruin surprises. They ruin the game itself since solving mysteries and puzzles is the whole point of the game.
I cannot even put into words how good this game was. Don't read anything about it other than the Steam page if it's not too late - the experience is well worth it. Favorite game by far.

What I liked the most about the game is the unique environments and how it is seamlessly connected.

It does require a lot of patience, but it's nice when you finally progress. You feel like you really are exploring. However, apart from that feeling of conquering a puzzle, there's not much reward usually. The late game is a bit frustrating since you'll run out of the assortment of things to explore and will probably have to repeat the same routine over and over again. I'm not the sharpest tool in the shed, but I only had to look at the solution for one obstacle, though I think I would eventually figured it out through trial and error, but I was a bit tired of the game after nearly 30 hours.

The story was quite meh, told mostly through text only. I wish there was at least some voice overs. I couldn't care less about the characters too.

The controls are kind of fun, to be honest. I didn't have a lot of trouble with it and think it was kind of a part of the challenge. The ship damaging mechanic was more of a nuisance then a challenge especially when you get scraped by stuff you couldn't see.

All in all, that is quite a unique game, but not everyone will enjoy it.

the best game i know by far, calling it a game is almost unjust you could call it a once in a lifetime experience.

The game's soundtrack really delivers a feeling of nostalgia and melancholy and I can't stop listening to it over and over again.

One of the best game of all time, the story is fantastic, the exploration and mysteries are immersives, the music is beautifull, i can only recommand !

Behind those first 15-30 minutes of frustrating controls sits one of the greatest indie titles ever created.

I don't think there's other games like this one. Played it once with a friend, then gently guided a friend through it a second time, then dove back in with even more friends for the DLC. A fun little story, a huge mystery and its many puzzles and mechanics to learn, and the amazing little soundtrack that I keep listening to.

It's a game that shows you "look, here's a world, you'll never guess what's around the corner", and you keep going to explore it more, learn more about it, debate with friends about what the meaning of what things are and why.

10/10 would get spooked again.
One of my favourite games of all time. A true gem, almost nothing like it. Its not for everyone, but for those who love to explore for the sake of it, will find a truly beautiful experience here

Sadly this game gives me the worst motion sickness >.< I wish I could gift it to someone else or get a refund :/ I'm sure the game itself is great, but I just couldn't play more than 20 mins before feeling very sick :( I don't recommend this game to people who have similar gaming motion sickness issues.

A beautiful story told through first person exploration in a crazy solar system reminiscent of The Little Prince. The story is pursued in time-limited sections, making this a great game to fill limited idle hours. There's no inflicted violence, though the character can damage their equipment and die (and in fact does so repeatedly as a normal part of progress through the story).

One of the best Games I've ever played - everything fits perfectly together and exploring is awesome.
Whats really cool about this game, which no one seems to mention, is, that the whole movement is physics based which makes it incredibly fun to jump around rotating planets.

Outer Wilds is one of those games for the wandering type. I was genuinely so engaged in its storytelling by just exploration and Text Logs. It Demands your curiosity, it respects your intelligence, and has a satisfying sense of progression to its mystery, and that is the entire point of the gameplay loop. This scratches an itch I haven't quite had since I was a boy leaving Kokiri Forest in Ocarina of Time for the first time. It's a cosmic, horrific, and beautiful concept of a game, and unlike anything I've ever experienced. I can't recommend this enough, give it a go, don't be afraid to take breaks for a while because it's pretty overwhelming once you unravel the secrets of this world. Good luck not using a guide, about 40 hours in, I caved for a few missing log entries. I love this game to pieces, but it will not hold your hand at all!
10/10 I hate that I will never be able to experience the first time playing this ever again.

Fantastic game. It will leave you up at night scratching your head wondering what to do next, but once an idea comes and it turns out to be right, it is an amazing feeling.
The DLC is also great, but it is slightly underwhelming in the universe building, and there is a fundamental question that you naturally get at the end of the DLC that is never answered and it really should be, but other than that it is a fun and unique experience.

I have never left a review before after 18 years on steam. Yet I needed to do it for the first time for this game.

I don't even know how to describe how I feel. It's like closing a book you've devoured but in a stronger way. If this game were a painting, I would hang it and cherish it with my eyes every single morning. It leaves an indelible mark.

Outer Wilds is a masterpiece.
Absolutely charming game that scratched my itch for space exploration in the most wonderful and unexpected way.
This game is an adventure, an experience, a set of reflections, and at the end of the road, it leaves your eyes drenched in tears.

Outer Wilds encapsulates why video games should be regarded as an art form no less than books, music, films, and other media. This piece of art utilizes every facet of the interactivity that video games provide to give the players a journey that will be remembered for the rest of their lives.

To me, Outer Wilds has given me an intriguing universe to explore, with its genius design where the power-ups are not items or stat boosts, but rather it's my own knowledge about the various planets that I gained through organic exploration. What will stick with me the most is the ending, and how beautifully it wraps the whole thing together. Please play this game, because there's literally nothing else like it.

In my opinion, Outer Wilds is a very special game. To me it represents a refreshing break in an almost universal modern day trend. In a sea of games that seek to iterate on existing design formulas, Outer Wilds stands out as a game that seeks to offer something new. Of course many (if not most) of Outer Wilds' design elements might have derived from existing games; Outer Wilds has a health bar, it has a jump button, it has seamless interplanetary travel, it has exploration (these are just a few examples). It's the way these elements have been assembled and tuned that manages to subvert expectations and contribute to an experience that is unlike any other. As a result, Outer Wilds feels powerfully deliberate. Elements of the game aren't slotted into a design formula; it seems as though each one was included to fill a carefully considered role.

Does any of that speak to Outer Wilds' quality? If not, I can make a separate assurance of that. I enjoyed the game a lot, and I believe it is competently constructed. If you're ever itching to experience a new Sci-Fi adventure, I suggest you consider the Outer Wilds. It delivers a story full of mystery, intrigue, beauty, emotion, alien technology, and most importantly: marshmallows. Give it a try or add it to your wishlist if you're even a little bit interested; it does not disappoint!

Gems like this are the reason video games are the superior medium. No cinematics, no gameplay elements that feel like a chore - straight to the point with immersive and well thought out gameplay used as a tool to tell a great story.

This is why games are great, not the unc*arteds, ass*assin creeds and the likes.

Go in as blind as you can.

Outer wilds is a solar system exploration game with a Groundhog day mechanic.
The time element seems irrelevant to the gameplay at first, but the planets actually change depending on how long into the time loop you are. This opens up for a ton of fun puzzles. If you ever get stuck on what to do on a puzzles i recommend exploring elsewhere, as you can find hints that may help you around the solar system.

As you explore you discover the history of a long lost civilization and the mystery of the repeating time loop.

The world design is great, Mastering the spaceship is a lot of fun and the music creates the perfect atmosphere(hohoho) for exploration.

I Heartily recommend this game. 10/10
Truly innovate, fun to explore. Lots of AHA moments. You should pick this up and be amazed. Plus, fund soundtrack. This game is a true masterpiece
Every so often there comes a game where you want to erase it from your mind just so you can play it for the first time all over again. This is one of those games.

Words can't express how much of an impact this game had on me, it revitalized my faith in the indie game genre and that games can induce genuine emotional impact without directly tugging on your heart strings.

Everything has a role and a purpose in such a well knitted experience that its impossible to not get invested in the world and lore and before you know it you just lose yourself in the breadcrumbs and then it ends how it begins with roasting marshmallows.

Legitimately in my top 20 games of all time easily.

Just an amazing game, one of the best on Steam. You should definitely play it spoiler-free.
Be aware, though: it's not an easy, casual game. You'll need to train in maneuvering the spaceship, and the 'puzzles' can be quite challenging, as the game offers little guidance on what you need to do.

One of the most novel and immersive video game experiences I've ever had. Incredibly immersive atmosphere, beautiful and dramatic sound effects, and engaging (and often lighthearted) visuals. Gameplay was unique; the cross between puzzle and adventure made it feel like a virtual puzzle room. Generally the game gave enough clues to figure out the next step. I did have to search out some help at some points in the game.

The Outer Wilds is one of the best games I have ever played. That's all I can say. If you feel compelled to be convinced, then what are you waiting for? An actual masterpiece that changed my life and thought processes. The feeling this experience gives is truly unmatched. Lightning in a bottle, once in a century type of game. No notes on what it could do or should do, it's incredible at doing everything on its own terms and not just the right way, but the only way. Please for the love of god go in completely blind and don't give up until you see those credits. You will thank yourself for it. My score cannot be understated:

10/10

What an incredible and beautiful piece of art.

If i had an option to erase my memory. This is the first game i will be playing. Over and over and over and over and over... until the innumerable possibilities burst.

Before I came to that conclusion, I have attempted this game twice when it came out. I dropped the game and thought it was boring mainly because the gameplay was: heavily text-based, zero-direction in an open-world (or solar system), relies only on your exploration skills, and more reading. Luckily five years later my interests and gaming habits have changed which allowed me to do a 3rd attempt (still blind) and I Immersed myself being the newest recruit of the Space Program. 

The heavy scientific and philosophical topics, music, emotions and just the whole journey were top-notch.

So this game is in my opinion one of the best 30+ hours i have spent in my gaming life.

First I was really confused and annoyed that my progress "resets" everytime I die. Then my mind slowly got the plot and it became more addicting to find new clues every minute I played.

Got the same exploratory feeling from subnautica but without the crafting inbetween. Makes the journey a good ammount shorter (15 Hours if you are reasonable smart) but not bloatet. You keep digging for more information to get rid of the "what the hell is going on"-feeling and is just sooo good.

graphics are cute, in some parts absolutly beautiful and performance is great. Never had a crash. Soundtrack is also great. Calming, dark and sometimes epically powerful. Always fitting the gameplay setting.

the overall thematic the story discribes is not for everyone but quite mindbending. Fans of SciFi, this is the place!

Great Game idea well executed.

This is mainly a game about exploration and discovery. There are a few puzzles to figure out as well. Great atmosphere, fun movement, cool planets to explore. Best played blind to not spoil the central mystery.

Outer wilds literally changed my point of view on life and the world.
An outstanding exploring game, with an incredible understanding of time, mechanics inside the universe and the pure drip of dopamine when you understand something new.

Understanding is the big point in general. A lot of times you can be afraid of the dark, of the things that lie ahead of you or things you simply don't know. But the moment you understand those things, you know how to use them, play with them or shoot yourself through the whole galaxy right into the sun.

One last important tip: Some people call it a Metroid-Brainia and they are right. You can play this game only once. You can run through this game without special speedrun skills or gameplay in around 20 minutes. But you need around 10 hours to find out how you do that. The moment you know, the game is done.

So don't spoil yourself on youtube, play it and have a great time! :D

One of the best games I've ever played! It's an amazing experience you can only really have once, and you need to have it. Avoid spoilers like the plague, and have fun exploring this absolutely amazing solar system in a way unlike any space game I've seen.

I really enjoyed this game, the story is great and I had a lot of fun figuring out how it all fit together. The gameplay is pretty unique and was easy to get into. I'd recommend this game to anyone who likes exploring in games and learning about a world.

after finishing this game, I deeply regret every single time I've gotten spoiled before getting to play it, no matter how big or small the spoiler was.
truly close to a 10/10 masterpiece

This game is a masterpiece. Everything about it is perfect — the story, the graphics, the gameplay, the puzzles, the music, and the atmosphere. It’s an unforgettable experience that stays with you long after you finish playing. I wish there were more games like this
❤️❤️❤️

The DLC is just as incredible, adding even more depth and mystery to an already amazing game

100/10

The most unique, memorable and exciting adventure in our short life time. A mix of intrigue with fear, dread and anxiety, yet so incredibly engaging that curiosity always prevails. Exploration at its finest.

Very fun game that has you explore the solar system to find out its secrets, such as what happened to the previous inhabitants, what they built, what they discovered and the strange situation you find yourself in.

If you like a game with an intriguing world and story that's told mostly through text left by the people before you and environmental storytelling with no combat, just flying/walking/exploring, then this is the game for you.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (95%): players love the story and characters, with music and art also praised.
A few find the gameplay tedious and boring.

details.text: Recent reviews complain less about story and gameplay, down to 3% each from 6% all time.
Reviewers with little playtime are split at 55% positive, while long-time players are strongly positive, so buyers who stay with it usually like it.
